description:
About Darkhorse Tech

Darkhorse Tech is a managed IT services provider built for dental. We support 1,500+ dental practices, specialists, multi-location groups, and DSOs nationwide with day-to-day IT support, cybersecurity, HIPAA compliance, cloud hosting, and email security. We are 100+ people who work almost entirely in one industry, which means we get good at it.

About This Role

We are hiring a Service Manager to own service delivery across our Service Team and our NOC.

Read that carefully, because it is the part most candidates miss. This is not a seat where you manage a help desk. You will manage five team leaders, four Technical Team Leaders and one NOC Team Lead, who together carry fifty-two people between them. Your job is not to solve tickets. It is to build five leaders who run their teams well, hold the same standards, and make good calls without asking you first.

If you are a strong technician who wants to keep touching the work, this is the wrong job. If you have managed managers before and you get satisfaction out of watching someone you coached handle something they could not have handled six months ago, keep reading.

What You'll Do

• Manage and develop four Technical Team Leaders and one NOC Team Lead through consistent one-on-ones, clear expectations, and real accountability

• Own the service KPIs across both organizations: response time, resolution time, CSAT, ticket aging, and backlog

• Make the experience consistent, so a client gets the same Darkhorse regardless of which pod takes the ticket, and a technician gets the same standards regardless of which lead they report to

• Oversee NOC operations including backup verification, email security, third-party vendor coordination, practice management software updates, and proactive monitoring, and keep NOC integrated with Service rather than running as a separate island

• Serve as the escalation point when a Team Leader cannot resolve a client issue, and then fix the reason it escalated

• Establish and enforce service processes, workflows, and documentation standards

• Partner with People and Culture on hiring, onboarding, performance, and retention across the service organization

• Carry quarterly ROCKs on our Service Traction Leadership Team

What We're Looking For

• Real experience managing managers. Not managing a team of technicians. Managing the people who manage the technicians. This is the single most important qualification.

• IT service leadership experience, ideally at an MSP

• Track record of moving service KPIs, and the ability to talk specifically about what you changed and what happened

• Comfort with NOC functions: backup verification, email security, monitoring

• Experience with multi-location or enterprise accounts. Our largest DSO clients expect a different level of consistency than a single practice does.

• Coaching instinct. You develop people rather than working around them.

• Analytical and process-driven. You look at the data before you look for someone to blame.

• Solid grounding in HIPAA, cybersecurity fundamentals, and ITIL principles

• PSA and RMM experience. ConnectWise preferred.

•Dental or healthcare IT background

• Familiarity with dental practice management software (Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental)

• Experience integrating a NOC function with a reactive service desk

•EOS or Traction experience

AI agents are starting to make decisions in regulated enterprises, including US banks and insurers. Factify turns an organization's policies, documents and real-world practice into a sealed, executable rulebook that governs how those agents decide. Every decision is traceable, auditable and ratified by the people who own the process.
The role
You will be our US insurance expert. You will map how critical decisions are really made inside US carriers, starting with how claims are adjudicated and how coverage is interpreted, and turn that judgment into explicit, testable rules. • Map claims processes end to end: first notice of loss, triage, coverage verification, investigation, adjudication, reserving, settlement and recovery.

• Analyze policy forms, endorsements, exclusions and claims manuals. Identify contradictions and ambiguity between documents and between documents and practice.

• Translate coverage interpretation and authority limits into structured rules, including SIU and fraud indicators, escalation triggers and state-mandated handling timelines.

• Build test cases and golden-label datasets (covered / not covered / refer, with evidence) across lines such as property, auto, health and liability.

• Review agent outputs against how experienced insurance professionals would decide, and document the failure modes.

• Work with customer leaders to ratify and maintain the rulebook over time.

Requirements

• 10+ years in insurance at a US carrier, TPA or MGA, with deep expertise in claims management, claims operations, coverage analysis or insurance compliance.

• Experience with process documentation, quality assurance or audit of insurance decisions.

• The ability to separate what the policy says from what the organization actually does, and to explain both clearly.

• Availability for regular overlap with our Tel Aviv team.

• Clear written and verbal communication with insurance leaders, executives and engineers.

• Location: Remote (US), with regular overlap with our Tel Aviv team (US Eastern morning hours).

Hands-on experience in any critical process inside an insurer. Every additional process you know from the inside widens the range of customer problems you can solve. Examples:

• Underwriting and risk selection

• Policy administration, endorsements and renewals

• Billing, premium collection and cancellations

• Fraud detection and SIU investigations

• Subrogation, salvage and recovery

• Reinsurance and ceded claims

• Reserving and actuarial processes

• Regulatory filings, market conduct and compliance

• Broker and agent management

• Customer service, complaints and litigation management

Nice to have

• Experience at an insurtech, in a claims-automation program or in a Big 4 insurance practice.

• Exposure to rules engines, core insurance platforms (such as Guidewire) or AI governance.

• CPCU, AIC, ARM or equivalent credentials.

Primary Skills: IAM Policy Templates, Cedar Policies
Role Overview:
Seeking an experienced Security Engineer with 15+ years of experience in cloud security and identity management to secure enterprise AI applications on AWS. The role focuses on authentication, reusable IAM policy templates, Cedar-based authorization, and secure access to tools, APIs, and enterprise resources.
Key Responsibilities
1. IAM Policy Templates & Access Management

• Design, develop, and maintain reusable AWS IAM policy templates for AI agents and AgentCore infrastructure.

• Implement role-based access control (RBAC) and least-privilege security principles.

• Define IAM roles, trust policies, permission boundaries, and resource-based policies.

• Configure IAM execution roles for AgentCore Runtime and AgentCore Gateway.

• Develop standardized IAM templates for accessing AWS services such as Lambda, S3, Bedrock, API Gateway, Secrets Manager, and CloudWatch.

• Automate IAM policy deployment and configuration using Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, or AWS CDK.

• Conduct IAM access reviews, permission audits, and policy validation.

• Troubleshoot access-denied issues, role-assumption failures, and authorization misconfigurations.

2. Cedar Policies at AgentCore Gateway

• Design, author, test, and deploy Cedar authorization policies using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy.

• Implement fine-grained authorization for AI agents accessing tools through AgentCore Gateway.

• Define policies specifying which identities can invoke particular tools, APIs, and operations.

• Configure policy engines and associate them with AgentCore Gateways.

• Implement attribute-based access control (ABAC) using identity attributes, roles, scopes, and contextual conditions.

• Develop policies that restrict sensitive tool operations based on business roles, permissions, and security requirements.

• Validate Cedar policies against gateway schemas and test permitted and denied access scenarios.

• Enforce default-deny authorization and prevent unauthorized tool execution.

• Monitor and troubleshoot authorization decisions and policy evaluation failures.

3. Security Governance & Compliance

• Implement security controls for enterprise AI agents and Generative AI applications.

• Develop security standards for agent identities, API integrations, and access management.

• Support audit logging, access traceability, and security monitoring using AWS CloudTrail and CloudWatch.

• Identify and mitigate risks including excessive privileges, credential exposure, unauthorized tool access, and privilege escalation.

• Conduct security reviews of agent architecture and integrations.

• Collaborate with AI engineering and DevOps teams to ensure secure production deployments.

4. Security Automation & DevSecOps

• Automate security policy deployment through GitHub Actions and infrastructure-as-code pipelines.

• Integrate IAM and Cedar policy validation into CI/CD workflows.

• Implement automated security checks and policy compliance testing.

• Maintain version-controlled security configurations across development, testing, and production environments.

• Support security incident investigation, access troubleshooting, and remediation.

AWS Security: IAM, IAM roles, policies, STS, AWS Secrets Manager, CloudTrail, CloudWatch.

•
Authorization: Cedar policy language, RBAC, ABAC, fine-grained access control.

•
Authentication: OAuth 2.0, OIDC, JWT, AWS IAM authentication.

Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, AWS CDK, or CloudFormation.

Automation: Python, GitHub Actions, CI/CD security integration.

description:
Join the team leading the next evolution of virtual care.
At Teladoc Health , you are empowered to bring your true self to work while helping millions of people live their healthiest lives.
Here you will be part of a high-performance culture where colleagues embrace challenges, drive transformative solutions, and create opportunities for growth. Together, we’re transforming how better health happens.
Summary of Position

The Manager, Release & Change Engineering is a hands-on technical leadership role that unifies Release Management and Change Management into a single engineering function. This role does not exist to process paperwork or maintain legacy processes. It exists to modernize how software and infrastructure releases / changes move safely and quickly from development to production. The successful candidate will be deeply fluent in CI/CD and deployment tooling, lead Change Advisory Board (CAB) with technical authority, and drive the shift from manual, meeting-based approvals to automated, risk-based controls embedded in the delivery pipeline.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Release Engineering

• Own the end-to-end software release process, including deployment sequencing and release-day decision authority.

• Serve as Release Manager for complex and high-risk releases, with direct accountability for go/no-go decisions.

• Lead production readiness reviews, validating deployment plans, rollback procedures, and environment gating before release.

• Run post-release retrospectives, track actions to closure, and convert findings into pipeline or process controls.

Change Governance and CAB

• Lead enterprise change management processes and governance activities.

• Chair the Change Advisory Board (CAB) with authority to challenge, table, or reject changes on technical grounds.

• Manage the full lifecycle of standard, emergency, expedited, and planned changes.

• Enforce control integrity: separation of duties between implementers and approvers, rollback readiness as a mandatory CAB gate, and accurate change-to-incident attribution, including batched deployments.

• Govern change freezes, change communications, and compliance with established processes.

Technical Risk and Failure Analysis

• Assess deployment and change-related risks and recommend mitigation strategies.

• Analyze failed changes to distinguish human error, process gaps, and technical failure modes, and drive corrective actions to closure with engineering owners.

• Partner with Incident Management on RCAs where change is a contributing factor, closing the loop between change risk and incident impact.

• Own the continuous improvement program for change and release engineering - using change failure data to inform CAB review criteria, Standard Change eligibility decisions, and deployment process improvements - partnering with platform teams to optimize testing, CI, and related tooling.

Transformation & Automation

• Lead a multi-year roadmap that moves change governance from manual, meeting-based review to risk-based, automated controls.

• Build change controls into the CI/CD pipeline, including pipeline-generated change records, automated risk scoring, evidence-based approvals, and deployment gates.

• Partner with Engineering teams - DevOps, etc. to strengthen deployment pipelines, test gating, and safer deployment patterns.

• Expand Standard Change and tiered pre-approval coverage, using change data to reduce CAB dependency for low-risk, high-frequency changes.

Metrics & Reporting

• Own release and change KPIs, including DORA-aligned change failure rate, lead time changes, deployment frequency, and failed-deployment recovery time, alongside CAB cycle time and Standard Change utilization.

• Develop dashboards and reporting to provide visibility into operational performance and trends.

• Present change and release health to engineering and SMO leadership with clear attribution and actionable recommendations.

- Experience with search, LLMs, or data-heavy products.

- Shooting Star Speed - We move with extreme speed. We value momentum, decisiveness, and the ability to accelerate when it matters.
